title: Drinking water total coliform (RTCR) practice questions
description: Free total coliform (RTCR) practice questions on 40 CFR 141 Subpart Y. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.topic: General provisions and laboratory methods
questions.question: What standard sample volume does 141.852(a)(1) set for total coliform analysis, regardless of the analytical method used?
questions.explanation: 141.852(a)(1): "The standard sample volume required for analysis, regardless of analytical method used, is 100 ml."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.852, Analytical methods and laboratory certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: General provisions and laboratory methods
questions.question: What limit does 141.852(a)(3) set on the time from sample collection to initiation of test medium incubation?

options.D: There is no limit if the sample is held below 10 deg. C

questions.explanation: "The time from sample collection to initiation of test medium incubation may not exceed 30 hours." Holding samples below 10 deg. C is "encouraged but not required".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.852, Analytical methods and laboratory certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Sample siting plans and sample validity
questions.question: Under 141.853(a)(2), which systems may collect all required total coliform samples on a single day, if the samples are taken from different sites?

options.A: Any community water system serving 10,000 or fewer people
options.B: Subpart H systems serving 1,000 or fewer people
options.C: Systems serving more than 4,900 people that use surface water
options.D: Systems that use only ground water and serve 4,900 or fewer people

questions.explanation: Samples go at regular intervals through the month, "except that systems that use only ground water and serve 4,900 or fewer people may collect all required samples on a single day if they are taken from different sites."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.853, General monitoring requirements for all public water systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Sample siting plans and sample validity
questions.question: Unless the alternatives in 141.853(a)(5)(i) or (ii) apply, where must a system take its repeat samples after a total coliform-positive sample?

options.A: At least one at the original tap and two at any other routine sampling sites
options.B: At least one at the original tap, one at a tap within five service connections upstream and one at a tap within five service connections downstream
options.C: At least one at the entry point to the distribution system and two at the original tap
options.D: At least one at a tap within ten service connections upstream and one within ten service connections downstream

questions.explanation: The system must collect "at least one repeat sample from the sampling tap where the original total coliform-positive sample was taken, and at least one repeat sample at a tap within five service connections upstream and at least one repeat sample at a tap within five service connections downstream of the original sampling site."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.853, General monitoring requirements for all public water systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Sample siting plans and sample validity
questions.question: Under 141.853(c)(1)(i), what may the laboratory establish that allows the State to invalidate a total coliform-positive sample?

options.A: That all repeat samples are total coliform-negative
options.B: That improper sample analysis caused the total coliform-positive result
options.C: That the sample was collected on a weekend
options.D: That the system has only one service connection

questions.explanation: The State may invalidate a total coliform-positive sample when "The laboratory establishes that improper sample analysis caused the total coliform-positive result." It "may not invalidate a total coliform-positive sample solely on the grounds that all repeat samples are total coliform-negative."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.853, General monitoring requirements for all public water systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Non-community ground water systems serving 1,000 or fewer
questions.question: What routine total coliform monitoring frequency does 141.854(b) set for a non-community water system serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water, when it is not a seasonal system and none of paragraphs (c) through (h) and (j) changes its schedule?

options.A: Each calendar quarter that the system provides water to the public
options.B: Each week that the system provides water to the public

questions.explanation: "Systems must monitor each calendar quarter that the system provides water to the public, except for seasonal systems or as provided under paragraphs (c) through (h) and (j) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.854, Routine monitoring requirements for non-community water systems serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Non-community ground water systems serving 1,000 or fewer
questions.question: A non-community ground water system serving 1,000 or fewer people is on annual monitoring and has one subpart Y monitoring violation, with no other listed event. What does 141.854(f) require?

options.A: Begin weekly monitoring the week following the event
options.B: Stop serving water until a Level 2 assessment is completed
options.C: Take one make-up sample and remain on annual monitoring
options.D: Begin quarterly monitoring the quarter following the event

questions.explanation: Under 141.854(f), "A system on annual monitoring that experiences the event identified in paragraphs (f)(5) of this section must begin quarterly monitoring the quarter following the event"; (f)(5) is "one subpart Y monitoring violation for a system on annual monitoring."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.854, Routine monitoring requirements for non-community water systems serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Community ground water systems serving 1,000 or fewer
questions.question: A community water system serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water is on reduced (quarterly) monitoring and loses its certified operator. What does 141.855(d)(1) require?

options.A: Return to monthly monitoring after a rolling 12-month period
options.B: Complete a Level 2 assessment within 30 days
options.C: Return to monthly monitoring the month following that loss
options.D: Stay on quarterly monitoring until the next sanitary survey

questions.explanation: "A system that loses its certified operator must return to monthly monitoring the month following that loss."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.855, Routine monitoring requirements for community water systems serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Community ground water systems serving 1,000 or fewer
questions.question: What floor does 141.855(d)(1) set when the State reduces the monitoring frequency of a community water system serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water?

options.C: No less than once every three years
options.D: No less than once every six years

questions.explanation: "The State may reduce the monitoring frequency from monthly monitoring to no less than quarterly monitoring" if the system meets the listed criteria.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.855, Routine monitoring requirements for community water systems serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Subpart H systems and systems serving more than 1,000
questions.question: Under 141.856(b), what routine total coliform monitoring frequency applies to a subpart H system serving 1,000 or fewer people, including a consecutive system?

options.A: Quarterly, once it has a clean compliance history for 12 months
options.B: Annually, after a State site visit equivalent to a Level 2 assessment
options.C: Quarterly, if it is in compliance with State-certified operator provisions

questions.explanation: "Subpart H systems of this part (including consecutive systems) must monitor monthly. Systems may not reduce monitoring."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.856, Routine monitoring requirements for subpart H public water systems serving 1,000 or fewer people (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Subpart H systems and systems serving more than 1,000
questions.question: Under 141.857(c), what must a subpart H system serving more than 1,000 people that does not practice filtration in compliance with subparts H, P, T and W do on each day its source water turbidity (measured as specified in 141.74(b)(2)) exceeds 1 NTU?

options.A: Collect three repeat samples at the entry point to the distribution system
options.B: Collect at least one total coliform sample near the first service connection
options.C: Double the number of routine samples for that month
options.D: Collect a coliform sample at the farthest point of the distribution system

questions.explanation: The system "must collect at least one total coliform sample near the first service connection each day the turbidity level of the source water, measured as specified in § 141.74(b)(2), exceeds 1 NTU."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.857, Routine monitoring requirements for public water systems serving more than 1,000 people (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Subpart H systems and systems serving more than 1,000
questions.question: What minimum number of total coliform samples per month does the table in 141.857(b) set for a public water system serving 3,000 people?
questions.explanation: The 141.857(b) table row "2,501 to 3,300" sets a minimum of 3 samples per month.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.857, Routine monitoring requirements for public water systems serving more than 1,000 people (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Repeat monitoring and E. coli testing
questions.question: After a sample is total coliform-positive, what minimum number of repeat samples does 141.858(a)(1) set for each total coliform-positive sample found?
questions.explanation: "The system must collect no fewer than three repeat samples for each total coliform-positive sample found."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.858, Repeat monitoring and E. coli requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Repeat monitoring and E. coli testing
questions.question: Absent a State extension, what deadline does 141.858(a)(1) set for collecting the set of repeat samples after a total coliform-positive sample?

options.A: Within 24 hours of collecting the original sample
options.B: Within 10 days of being notified of the positive result
options.C: Within 30 days of being notified of the positive result
options.D: Within 24 hours of being notified of the positive result

questions.explanation: "The system must collect a set of repeat samples within 24 hours of being notified of the positive result." The State may extend this case by case for a logistical problem beyond the system's control.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.858, Repeat monitoring and E. coli requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Repeat monitoring and E. coli testing
questions.question: A total coliform-positive culture is found to contain E. coli, and the system is notified while the State office is open. Under 141.858(b)(1), when must the system notify the State?

options.A: Within 10 days after the system is notified
options.B: By the end of the day when the system is notified of the test result
options.C: Within 30 days after the system is notified
options.D: With the next monthly monitoring report

questions.explanation: "If E. coli are present, the system must notify the State by the end of the day when the system is notified of the test result"; the next-business-day option applies only when the State office is closed without an after-hours line or alternative procedure.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.858, Repeat monitoring and E. coli requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Treatment technique triggers and assessments
questions.question: A system takes 50 total coliform samples per month. Under 141.859(a)(1)(i), what sample result is its Level 1 treatment technique trigger?

options.A: Exceeding 10.0% total coliform-positive samples for the month
options.C: Exceeding 5.0% total coliform-positive samples for the month
options.D: Exceeding 1.0% total coliform-positive samples for the month

questions.explanation: "For systems taking 40 or more samples per month, the system exceeds 5.0% total coliform-positive samples for the month."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.859, Coliform treatment technique triggers and assessment requirements for protection against potential fecal contamination (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Treatment technique triggers and assessments
questions.question: Which event does 141.859(a)(2) list as a Level 2 treatment technique trigger?

options.B: A single total coliform-positive routine sample
options.C: One missed routine sample in a compliance period
options.D: A source water turbidity reading above 1 NTU

questions.explanation: The Level 2 triggers include "An E. coli MCL violation, as specified in § 141.860(a)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.859, Coliform treatment technique triggers and assessment requirements for protection against potential fecal contamination (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Treatment technique triggers and assessments
questions.question: What deadline does 141.859(b)(3)(i) set for submitting the completed Level 1 assessment form to the State?

options.A: Within 24 hours after the system learns that it has exceeded a trigger
options.B: Within 30 days after the system learns that it has exceeded a trigger
options.C: By the end of the next business day after the trigger
options.D: Within one year after the trigger

questions.explanation: "The system must submit the completed Level 1 assessment form to the State within 30 days after the system learns that it has exceeded a trigger."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.859, Coliform treatment technique triggers and assessment requirements for protection against potential fecal contamination (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Violations, reporting and recordkeeping
questions.question: Which situation does 141.860(a) list as a violation of the MCL for E. coli?

options.A: The system has one total coliform-positive routine sample in which E. coli are not present
options.B: The system fails to take every required routine sample in a compliance period
options.C: The system fails to submit a completed assessment form after properly conducting the assessment
options.D: The system fails to take all required repeat samples following an E. coli-positive routine sample

questions.explanation: 141.860(a)(3): "The system fails to take all required repeat samples following an E. coli-positive routine sample." Missing routine samples is a monitoring violation and a late assessment form is a reporting violation.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.860, Violations (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Violations, reporting and recordkeeping
questions.question: What deadline does 141.861(a)(4) set for a system to report a coliform monitoring violation to the State?

options.A: By the end of the day the system discovers the violation
options.B: Within 48 hours after the system discovers the violation
options.C: Within 10 days after the system discovers the violation
options.D: Within 90 days after the system discovers the violation

questions.explanation: A system that failed a coliform monitoring requirement "must report the monitoring violation to the State within 10 days after the system discovers the violation, and notify the public in accordance with subpart Q of this part."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.861, Reporting and recordkeeping (as of Nov 3, 2026)
